title: セイバールート一日目-03

pages.ja:
「一成、いるか？」
「いるぞ。今朝は少し遅かったな、衛宮」
予習でもしていたのか、ペーパーらしきものに目を通していた男子生徒が顔をあげる。

pages.en:
“Issei, are you here?”

“I am. You're a little late this morning, Emiya.”

Perhaps he was studying. The male student looks up from the papers he had been reading.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Issei, you there?”
“I am. You’re a bit late today, Emiya.”
He must have been studying, as Issei looks up from the paper he’s reading.

pages.ja:
「一成だけか。他の連中はどうしたんだ。この時間なら登校しててもおかしくないだろ」
「いや、生憎とうちのメンバーはビジネスライクでね。
働く時間帯はきっかり決まっていて、早出と残業はしたくないのだそうだ」
「それで生徒会長自らが雑用か。ここはここで大変そうだな」

pages.en:
“Are you the only one here? What happened to everyone else? It wouldn't be strange for them to have arrived by now.”

“Unfortunately, the other members conduct themselves on strictly professional terms.

“Their working hours are precisely defined, and they have no desire to arrive early or perform overtime.”

“So the student council president handles all the menial work himself. You have your own troubles here.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Just you, Issei? Where are the others? Shouldn’t they be here now as well?”
“No. Unfortunately, our members are very businesslike.
They have their set work hours, and they don’t want to come in early or stay late.”
“That’s why the student council president is doing the routine duties himself, huh? I guess this place has its own problems.”

pages.ja:
「なに、好きでしている苦労だ。衛宮に同情してもらうのは筋が違う」
「？ いや、一成に同情なんてしてないぞ？」
「うむ、それはそれで無念だが聞き流すとしよう。情が移っているという事では同じだからな」
pages.jaRuby:
「なに、好きでしている苦労だ。[ruby text=えみや char=2]衛宮に同情してもらうのは筋が違う」

「うむ、それはそれで無念だが聞き流すとしよう。情が移っているという事では同じだからな」
pages.en:
“The burden is one I assume willingly. It would be improper to receive sympathy from you, Emiya.”

“? I wasn't sympathizing with you, Issei.”

“Hm. That is disappointing in its own way, but I shall let it pass. Either way, you care enough for the result to be the same.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“No, it’s the kind of trouble I like. You don’t need to pity me.”
“Huh? Uh, no, I wasn’t pitying you or anything.”
“Hm. I’m not happy about that either, but I’ll pretend I didn’t hear it. It still means that you care.”

pages.ja:
トントン、と読んでいたペーパーを整える一成は、この生徒会室の大ボスだ。
緩みきっている生徒会を根本から改革しようと躍起になっているヤツで、自分とは一年の頃からの友人である。
フルネームを柳洞一成。
古くさい名前とは裏腹に優雅な顔立ちをしていて、実際女生徒に絶大な人気がある。
しかも生徒会長だっていうんだから、まさに鬼に金棒、虎に翼といったところなのだが、

pages.en:
Issei taps the papers into order upon the desk. He is the big boss of this student council room.

We have been friends since our first year. He has devoted himself to reforming our thoroughly lax student council from its foundations.

His full name is Issei Ryuudou.

Despite that antiquated name, his features are elegant, and in fact he enjoys tremendous popularity among the female students.

Add the office of student council president, and it should be like placing an iron club in an ogre's hand—or granting wings to a tiger. And yet—
pages.mirrorMoon:
Issei, who is organizing the papers he was reading, is the big boss of this student council room.
He’s the guy trying his best to reform this lax student council, and he’s been a friend of mine since first year.
His full name is Ryuudou Issei.
Despite his old-fashioned name, he has elegant features and he’s really popular with the girls.
And he’s also the student council president, so you’d think he’d take to it like a duck to water, but…

pages.ja:
「うむ、やはり朝は舌がしびれる程の熱湯がよい」
なんて言いながら番茶をすすっているもんだから、いまいち締まらない。

pages.en:
“Hm. Scalding tea that numbs the tongue truly is the only proper drink in the morning.”

He says things like that while sipping bancha, which rather spoils the effect.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hm. Hot tea is certainly a good way to start a morning.”
He’s just sipping tea like this, so he’s not that firm.

pages.ja:
この通り、一成はとことん地味な性格だ。
誤解されやすいのだが、本人は色恋沙汰には手を出さないし、学生らしい遊びもしない。
なにしろコイツはお山にある柳洞寺の跡取り息子だ。
本人も寺を継ぐのを良しとしているので、卒業したら潔く丸坊主にする可能性も大である。

pages.en:
As this demonstrates, Issei is thoroughly sober and unassuming.

People often misunderstand him, but he has no interest in romance and indulges in none of the amusements customary among students.

He is, after all, the heir to Ryuudou Temple on the mountain.

He is content to inherit the temple. There is every possibility that upon graduating, he will shave his head without a moment's regret.
pages.mirrorMoon:
As you can see, Issei has a plain personality.
It’s easily misunderstood, but he doesn’t involve himself in love affairs nor engage in normal student recreations.
It’s because he’s the successor of the Ryuudou Temple, up in the mountains.
He’s fine with that idea, so there’s a good chance he’ll shave his head when he graduates.

pages.ja:
「それで。今日は何をするんだ」
「ん？ ああ、まあともかく座って一服
と言いたいのだが時間がないな。移動がてら説明をする故、いつもの道具を持って付いてきてくれ」

pages.en:
“Well then. What are we doing today?”

“Hm? Ah, yes. Ordinarily I would first invite you to sit and take tea—but we have no time. I will explain as we walk, so bring your usual tools and follow me.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“So, what am I doing today?”
“Hm? Well, I’d like to let you sit down and take a rest first… but I guess we don’t have time. I’ll explain as we go, so bring your usual tools and follow me.”

pages.ja:
「率直に言うとな。うちの学校、金のバランスが極端なんだよ」
「知ってる。運動系が贔屓されてるもんで、他に予算がいかないんだろ」
「うむ。結果、文化系の部員はたえず不遇の扱いでな。
今年から文化系に予算がいくよう尽力しているのだが、予算の流れが不鮮明でうまく回っていない。おかげで未だ文化系の部室は不遇でな。
とくに冬のストーブ不足に関しては打開策がまるでない」

「率直に言うとな。うちの学校、金のバランスが極端なんだよ」

とくに冬のストーブ不足に関しては打開策がまるでない」
pages.en:
“To be perfectly direct, our school's finances are grotesquely unbalanced.”

“I know. The athletic clubs receive special treatment, so there's no money left for anyone else.”

“Precisely. The members of our cultural clubs live in a state of perpetual deprivation.

“Since taking office, I have labored to direct more funding toward them, but the existing flow of money is opaque and resists reform. Their clubrooms continue to suffer.

“In particular, we possess no conceivable solution to the shortage of heaters this winter.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Frankly, our school’s budget is completely unbalanced.”
“I know. The athletic clubs are favored, so other clubs don’t get much, right?”
“Right. As a result, members of the other clubs are in trouble.
I’m working hard to make the budget go to them, but I’m having trouble because it’s not clear where the money’s going.
In particular, there’s no solution for the shortages of heaters during winter.”

pages.ja:
「そうか。
あ、マイナスドライバーくれ。一番おっきいヤツな。あと導線も。……うん、これぐらいならなんとか」
「導線？ ……えっと、これか？ すまん、よく判らん。
間違っていたら叱ってくれ」
「あたってるからいいよ。で、ストーブ不足がどうしたって？ ここ以外にも故障してんのがあんのか」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“I see. —Hand me the flathead screwdriver. The largest one. And some wire too. …Yes, I think I can manage this.”

“Wire? …Is this what you mean? Forgive me, I know very little about such things. Rebuke me if I am wrong.”

“That's the right one. So what about the heater shortage? Are there broken ones somewhere besides here?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I see. Oh, can you hand me the torque screwdriver? The biggest one. And the conductive wire too. …Yeah, I should be able to fix this.”
“Conductive wire? …Uh, is this it? Sorry, I don’t know exactly.
Tell me if I’m wrong.”
“You’re right. So, what was that about the shortage of heaters? Are there other broken ones?”

pages.ja:
「ある。第二視聴覚室と美術部の暖房器具が怪しいそうだ。新品購入願いの嘆願書が刻一刻と増えている」
「けど予算にそんな余裕はない、と。……やっぱり劣化してるだけだな。中がイカレてなくて助かった」
pages.jaRuby:

「けど予算にそんな余裕はない、と。……やっぱり劣化してるだけだな。中がイカレてなくて助かった」
pages.en:
“There are. I am told the heating devices in the second audiovisual room and the art club are behaving suspiciously. Petitions demanding replacements multiply by the hour.”

“But there's no room in the budget. …This one has only deteriorated. We're lucky nothing inside it is ruined.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Yes. In the 2nd AV room and the art club. The petitions requesting new stoves are multiplying.”
“But there’s not enough budget to meet the demand, huh? As I thought, it’s just getting old. Good thing it’s not broken on the inside.”

pages.ja:
「……ふむ。直りそうか、衛宮？」
「直るよ。こういう時、古いヤツは判りやすくていい。
配線系のショートだから新しいのに替えれば、とりあえず今年いっぱいは頑張ってくれる」
「そうか！ やるな衛宮、おまえが頼りになると極めて嬉しいぞ」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“…Hm. Can you repair it, Emiya?”

“Yes. Old machines are nice at times like this. They're easy to understand.

“The wiring shorted. Replace it, and this thing should struggle through the rest of the year.”

“I see! Excellent, Emiya. Nothing pleases me more than discovering how useful you are.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Hm. You think it can be fixed, Emiya?”
“Yup. In cases like this, old things are nice because they’re easy to understand.
It’s just a shorted connection, so it should last the whole year if we replace that.”
“I see! Good job, Emiya. I’m always so pleased when you’re reliable.”

pages.ja:
「おかしな日本語使うね、一成。
……っと、もう少しで済むから、ちょっと外に出ててくれ」
「うむ、衛宮の邪魔はせん」
pages.jaRuby:
「おかしな日本語使うね、一成。
……っと、もう少しで済むから、ちょっと外に出ててくれ」

pages.en:
“You phrase things strangely, Issei.

“…There. I'm almost finished, so wait outside for a moment.”

“Very well. I shall not interfere with your work.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“You’re wording it weirdly, Issei…
Oh, I’ll be finished soon, so could you wait outside for a bit?”
“All right, I’ll be out of your way.”

pages.ja:
静かに教室から出ていく一成。
……どうも、ここから先はデリケートな作業だと勘違いしたみたいだ。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
Issei leaves the classroom without a sound.

…Apparently, he mistook what comes next for some delicate operation.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Issei leaves the room quietly.
…It seems he assumes that I’m going to do something delicate.

pages.ja:
「……いや、デリケートと言えばデリケートなんだけど……」
古びた電気ストーブに手を触れる。
普通、この手の修理に慣れているからと言って、見るだけでは故障箇所は判断できない。
それが判るという事は、俺のやっている事は普通じゃないってことだ。

“…Well, I suppose it is delicate in its own way…”

I place my hand upon the old electric heater.

Ordinarily, experience repairing appliances would not let anyone identify a fault merely by looking.

The fact that I can do so means what I am doing is not ordinary.

pages.ja:
視覚を閉じて、触覚でストーブの中身を視る。
途端。
頭の中に湧き上がってくる一つのイメージ。
pages.jaRuby:

頭の中に湧き上がってくる一つのイメージ。
pages.en:
I close my eyes to sight and use touch to *see* the heater's interior.

—At once—

A single image rises within my mind.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I block off my vision and look inside the heater with my sense of touch.
In that moment…
An image appears in my head.

pages.ja:
「……電熱線が断線しかかってるのが二つと……電熱管はまだ保つな……電源コードの方は絶縁テープでなんとかなる……」
……良かった、手持ちの工具だけで修理できる破損内容だ。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“…Two of the heating wires are nearly severed… The element will hold a while longer… Insulating tape should take care of the power cord…”

…Good. The damage can be repaired with the tools I have.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…There are two places where the wire’s about to break… The pipe should last a bit longer… Insulation tape should be enough for the power cord…”
…Good, I can fix this with the tools I have with me.

pages.ja:
電熱管がイカレていたら素人の手には負えない。
その時は素人じゃない方法で“強化”しなくてはいけなかったが、これなら内部を視るだけで十分だ。
それが切嗣に教わった、衛宮士郎の“魔術”である。

pages.en:
If the heating element itself had failed, an amateur could do nothing with it.

I would have needed to employ the decidedly unamateur method of “Reinforcement.” As things stand, simply seeing the interior is enough.

That is the “magecraft” Kiritsugu taught to Shirou Emiya.
pages.mirrorMoon:
If the pipe were broken, it couldn’t be fixed by an amateur.
If that had been the case, I would have had to “strengthen” it in a very unamatuerish way. But in this case, just looking at it will suffice.
That is the “magic” Emiya Shirou learned from Kiritsugu.

破損箇所はもう判っているんだから、あとの作業は簡単だ。
「……はあ。これだけは得意なんだけどな、俺」

pages.en:
“—All right. Let's begin.”

I remove the casing and set to work upon the internal wiring.

I already know where the damage lies. The remaining work is simple.

“…Sigh. This is the one thing I'm good at.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“All right, let’s begin.”
I take the cover off and start to work.
I already know where it’s broken, so the rest is easy.
“…Man. This is the only thing I’m any good at.”

pages.ja:
そう。衛宮士郎に魔術の才能はまったく無かった。
その代わりといってはなんだが、物の構造、さっきみたいに設計図を連想する事だけはバカみたいに巧いと思う。
実際、設計図を連想して再現した時なんて、親父は目を丸くして驚いた後、「なんて無駄な才能だ」なんて嘆いていたっけ。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
Yes. Shirou Emiya possesses no talent for magecraft whatsoever.

In compensation, if it can be called that, I have a ridiculous gift for grasping an object's structure—for calling to mind a blueprint as I did a moment ago.

When I first reproduced such a blueprint, the old man stared in astonishment before lamenting, “What an utterly useless talent.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
That’s right. Emiya Shirou has no talent for magic.
Though it doesn’t make up for it, I think I’m quite skilled at visualizing structures like I did just now.
In fact, when I first figured out a structure and reproduced it, my father looked surprised and said “what a useless ability”.

pages.ja:
俺の得意分野は、あまり意味のある才能ではないそうだ。
親父曰く、物の構造を視覚で捉えている時点で無駄が多い。
本来の魔術師なら、先ほどのようにわざわざ隅々まで構造を把握する、なんていう必要はない。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
Apparently my particular aptitude serves little purpose.

According to the old man, perceiving an object's structure visually is already wasteful.

A proper mage would never need to laboriously comprehend every corner of an object as I did.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I guess my strong point isn’t a useful ability.
According to my father, it’s already a waste of effort to perceive the structure with my eyes.
For a real magus, there’s no need to understand every corner of a structure like I just did.

pages.ja:
物事の核である中心を即座に読みとり、誰よりも速く変化させるのが魔術師たちの戦いだと言う。
だから設計図なんてものを読みとるのは無駄な手間だし、読みとったところで出来る事といったら魔力の通りやすい箇所が判る程度の話。

物事の核である中心を即座に読みとり、誰よりも速く変化させるのが魔術師たちの戦いだと言う。
だから設計図なんてものを読みとるのは無駄な手間だし、読みとったところで出来る事といったら魔力の通りやすい箇所が判る程度の話。
pages.en:
A mage's battle consists of instantly reading the central core of a thing and altering it faster than anyone else.

Reading its entire blueprint is wasted effort. Even after doing so, all one learns is where magical energy will pass through it most readily.
pages.mirrorMoon:
They say that the battle of the magus comes in reading the center, the core of things instantaneously, and changing it faster than anything else.
That’s why reading the structure is a wasted effort, as even if you do understand the structure, all you can do is determine where magical energy could be more easily transmitted.

pages.ja:
そんなこんなで、自分の得意な分野はこういった故障品の修理だったりする訳だ。
なにしろ解体して患部を探し出す必要がない。
すみやかに故障箇所を探し出せるなら、あとは直す技術を持っていれば大抵の物は直せるだろう。
ま、それもこういった『ちょっとした素人知識』で直せてしまうガラクタに限るのだが。

pages.en:
Thus the field in which my talent proves useful is repairing broken objects like this one.

I do not have to dismantle them to locate the wound.

If I can find the fault immediately, then as long as I possess the skill to mend it, I can repair almost anything.

Though only when the junk in question can be restored with the sort of modest amateur knowledge I possess.
pages.mirrorMoon:
So all in all, it turns out that my strong point is just in fixing things like this.
I don’t have to open them up to look for damage.
If I can quickly search for broken parts and have the skills to repair them, most things can be fixed.
Though, that’s only the case for simple things that can be fixed with “amateur knowledge”.

廊下には、一成の他にもう一人、女生徒の姿があった。

“Issei, the repair is finished.”

—And then I notice.

Another student is standing in the corridor with him.

But.

“————”

I am mildly surprised.

The girl speaking to Issei is Rin Tohsaka of Class 2-A.

She is a young lady of means who lives in the particularly large Western mansion at the top of the hill—and an honor student so perfect that the fact borders on absurdity.

Beautiful, brilliant, gifted at every sport, and apparently without a single flaw.

Her manner is intelligent and courteous, and she never trades upon her beauty. In short, they say she is every boy's ideal woman.

“”

The person talking to Issei is Tohsaka Rin, from class 2-A.
She’s a lady who lives in a big mansion on top of the hill, a perfect honor student.
Good looking, smart, athletic, and faultless.
She’s intelligent, well mannered, and modest about her looks. People say she’s the ideal woman.

pages.ja:
そんなヤツだから、言うまでもなく男子生徒にとってはアイドル扱いだ。

遠坂と話が出来るのは一成と先生たちぐらいなもの、というのが男どもの通説だ。

It goes without saying that the male students treat someone like her as an idol.

But in Tohsaka's case, she is so perfect that she has become unapproachable.

Popular wisdom among the boys holds that only Issei and the teachers are capable of speaking to her.

So it hardly needs to be said that the guys at my school treat her like an idol.
Though in Tohsaka’s case, she’s so perfect that she’s considered unreachable.
It’s commonly believed that only teachers and guys like Issei can even talk to her.

pages.ja:
……まあ、正直に言えば、俺だって男だし。
ご多分に漏れず、自分も遠坂凛に憧れている男子生徒の一人である。

“……”

Impressive.

Issei begins speaking while ignoring Tohsaka completely. The man has courage.

“Don't worry about it. Where are we going next? We don't have much time.”

「天寿、全うしてたら直せないだろ。買い直した方が早いぞ」
「……そうなんだが、一応見てくれると助かる。俺から見れば臨終だが、おまえから見れば仮病かもしれん」
pages.jaRuby:
「天寿、全うしてたら直せないだろ。買い直した方が早いぞ」
「……そうなんだが、一応見てくれると助かる。俺から見れば臨終だが、おまえから見れば仮病かもしれん」
pages.en:
“If it completed its natural lifespan, I can't repair it. Buying another would be quicker.”

“…True. But I would appreciate it if you looked. To my eyes it is on its deathbed; to yours, it may merely be malingering.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It can’t be fixed if it’s dead. It would be quicker to just buy a new one.”
“…True, but it’d help if you could take a look at it. It might be dead to my eyes, but only faking it to yours.”

直すのなら急がないと間に合わないだろう。

If I mean to repair it, I must hurry.

“I see. Well, let’s take a look.”

I’ll have to hurry if I’m going to fix it.

“You're here early, Tohsaka.”

I voice the simple observation and follow Issei away.

“What a guy. How can he talk like that when he’s the one who drove you out?”
“Oh, you were here, Issei?”
“What do you mean!? You’re so cold, saying that to a friend who was listening in out of concern!”

“? Why would that be thoughtful? I didn't do anything you needed to worry about.”

pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hm? Why would you do that? I’m not doing anything that should make you worry about me.”
“Idiot. Of course I’ll worry about you. You’re the sort to lose your temper easily. Some people would cheer if you beat Shinji up, but all the girls would condemn you. It’s not good to let a friend get into a situation like that.”

pages.ja:
「そっか。うん、言われてみればそうだ。ありがとう一成。そんなコトにはならないだろうけど、今の心配はありがたい」

“Good. Your understanding is sufficient. …Still, I am surprised. You are easily angered, yet remarkably tolerant of Matou.”

“That behavior is simply Shinji's particular flavor. After knowing him long enough, you become accustomed to it.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I see. You’re right now that you mention it. Thanks, Issei. I don’t think it’ll be a problem, but I’m grateful for your concern.”
“Yes, well, as long as you understand… but it’s strange. You lose your temper easily, but you’re tolerant of Matou.”
“Yeah, that’s just his style. You get used to it if you hang around him for a long time.”

pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hm, I see.”

“Haha. It’s more like her to come floating in than flying in.”

The bell marking the beginning of homeroom rings.

The homeroom bell rings.

For Class 2-C, homeroom begins approximately one minute after the bell—

—with the thunder of Fuji charging down the corridor at full speed.

The transition is almost violently abrupt.

As expected of Fuji. She did not earn the name “human roller coaster” by halves.

“”

A sudden change of atmosphere.
Just as you’d expect from Fuji-nee. Her nickname of “human jet coaster” isn’t just for show.

藤ねえは教壇に頭をぶつけたまま倒れている。

Fuji lies with her head against the teacher's platform.

She has fallen facedown, hiding her expression and forcing every possible nightmare upon our imaginations.

…But that really was a bad hit.
Fuji-nee is still on the ground, having hit her head on the platform.
You can’t see her expression with her head facing the ground, so it gives you a bad mental image.

Everyone here is a veteran who has survived a full year with Fuji.

Perhaps they all feel it is past time we abolish the custom of carrying our homeroom teacher to the infirmary.

Everyone here is a warrior who has been with Fuji-nee for the past year.

Fuji does not twitch.

A sense of worry runs through the room.

“Fujimura-sensei, Fujimura-sensei…! It’s no good, there’s no response…!”

“Ms. Fujimura, if you don't wake up, you're a Tiger!”

“Don't lose, Tiger! Rise again, Tiger!”

“Come on, wake up, Ms. Fujimura! Show us you're a real Tiger!”

“Ti-ger! Ti-ger!”

“Don’t give up, Tiger! Stand up, Tiger!”
“Yeah, wake up, Sensei! Then you’ll be a true Tiger!”
“T-i-g-e-r! T-i-g-e-r!”

pages.en:
A thunderbolt splits the heavens.

Apparently the impact harmed her not at all. Fuji rises magnificently from the earth.
pages.mirrorMoon:
A roar of lightning.
She stands bravely as if the fall has done nothing at all.

……どうも、教室に飛び込んできてから立ち上がるまでの記憶が、ポッカリ抜け落ちているようだ。

“…Hm? What are all of you doing? You mustn't leave your seats during homeroom. Come on, sit down. We're beginning now.”

Fuji takes her place at the front as though nothing happened.

…Apparently everything between her entrance and her return to consciousness has vanished cleanly from her memory.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Huh? What are you all doing? You can’t stand up in middle of homeroom. Come on, sit down and I’ll get started.”
Fuji-nee stands before everyone in her usual manner.
…It seems all memories from the moment she entered the classroom have fled her head.

pages.ja:
「……おい、タイガー覚えてないみたいだぞ」
「……ラッキー、朝からついてるな、俺たち」
「……いや、ついてるっていうのかな、こういうの……」
ガヤガヤとそれぞれの席に戻る生徒たち。

pages.en:
“…Hey, I don't think Tiger remembers.”

“…Lucky. The day's going our way already.”

“…Does this truly qualify as good luck…?”

The students return noisily to their desks.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Hey, it seems Tiger doesn’t remember what happened.”
“…Lucky. We’re really fortunate this morning.”
“…Well, I don’t know if we can call it ‘lucky’…”
Everyone returns to their seats, chatting.

「いえ、してないっすよ。気のせいじゃないっすか」
「そっか、ならよし。じゃあ今朝のホームルームをはじめるから、みんな大人しく聞くように」

“Nope. Must've been your imagination.”

“Oh, all right. Then we'll begin morning homeroom. Everyone listen quietly.”

“All right, good. Then I’ll start homeroom, so listen up.”

Fuji begins homeroom at her leisure.

She wanders into idle conversation between every minor announcement, so it makes no progress at all.

“What? Six is practically right away! Miss Taiga, can't you exempt the athletic clubs?”

It’s at six o’clock, so people with club activities shouldn’t stay too late either.”
“What? Six o’clock is too early, Taiga-sensei. Can’t the athletic clubs be exempted?”

“I cannot! And Gotou, you must call me Ms. Fujimura. If you use my given name again, I'll become angry. Understood?”

“Yes, ma'am. I'll be careful from now on.”

Gotou returns to his seat with the unmistakable air of someone who will exercise no caution whatsoever.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Nope. And Gotou-kun, please address your teacher as ‘Fujimura-sensei’. I’ll get mad if you call me that again.”
“All right, I’ll be careful.”
Gotou-kun sits down again, not showing any signs of listening to her.

pages.ja:
……なんて甘い。
藤ねえは怒るといったら怒る人だ。相手が生徒だろうが自分が教師だろうが関係ない。
今のは限りなく本気に近い最後通牒なんだって、後藤のヤツ気づいていない。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
…How naive.

When Fuji says she will become angry, she means it. It makes no difference whether the other person is a student or she is supposed to be a teacher.

Gotou does not realize that her warning was as close to a genuine final ultimatum as one can come.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…How stupid of him.
Fuji-nee gets mad when she says she will. It makes no difference that he’s a student and she’s a teacher.
He doesn’t realize that she just gave him a final warning.

pages.ja:
「それじゃ今日のホームルームはここまで。みんな、三時限目の英語で会おうねー！」
手のひらをヒラヒラさせて去っていく藤ねえ。

“That concludes today's homeroom. I'll see all of you in third-period English!”

Fuji waves and strolls from the classroom.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Well, that’s it for today’s homeroom. Let’s meet again in English class in third period, everyone!”
Fuji-nee leaves, waving her hand.

Taiga Fujimura, homeroom teacher of Class 2-C.

Nickname: Tiger.

It sounds too absurd to be real, but reality offers us no choice in the matter.
pages.mirrorMoon:
She’s the teacher responsible for class 2-C, Fujimura Taiga.
Her nickname is Tiger.
You might doubt it, but it really is her nickname.

藤ねえ曰く、女の子らしくない、とかなんとか。
けど本人がああいう人なんで、あだ名が女の子らしくないのは当然というか自業自得だろう。

pages.en:
People call her that affectionately because her given name is Taiga, but Fuji herself despises the nickname Tiger.

According to her, it isn't feminine enough, or something like that.

Given the kind of person she is, however, the lack of femininity in her nickname seems both inevitable and entirely self-inflicted.
pages.mirrorMoon:
People like calling her so since she has a name like “Taiga”. But Fuji-nee herself hates the nickname.
According to her, it’s unfeminine.
But she’s that kind of person, so I think it’s her own fault she has an unfeminine nickname.

そうして、藤ねえと入れ違いで一時限目の先生が入ってくる。
藤ねえが時間ギリギリまでホームルームをするせいで、うちのクラスの朝はいつもこんな感じだった。

pages.en:
“We will begin class. Class representative, lead the bow.”

As Fuji departs, the teacher for first period enters.

Because she stretches homeroom to the last possible moment, mornings in our class always begin this way.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“We’re starting class. Day monitor, the bows.”
The teacher for the first period enters as Fuji-nee exits.
It’s like this every morning, as Fuji-nee continues homeroom until the very last minute.

pages.ja:
そうして、いつも通り一日の授業が終了した。
部活動にいそしむ生徒、早足で帰宅する生徒、用もなく教室に残る生徒、そのあり方は様々だ。
自分はと言うと、その三つのどれにも該当しそうにない。

pages.en:
And so the school day ends as uneventfully as ever.

Some students devote themselves to their clubs. Some hurry home. Some linger in the classroom for no reason at all.

As for me, I seem to belong to none of those three groups.
pages.mirrorMoon:
And the classes end like every other day.
There are many kinds of students: ones that go to clubs, ones that hurry home, and ones that stay in the classroom for no reason.
It looks like I won’t be in any of those categories.

そもそも弓道部を辞めた一番の理由は、アルバイトを優先したからだ。

“Forgive me, Emiya. Do you have a moment? This concerns the work from this morning. Are you free today?”

“Well, I do have plans of a sort.”

It is not as though I lead a life of leisure.

The principal reason I left the archery club was to give priority to my part-time work.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Sorry, Emiya, about the rest of the repairs… do you have time today?”
“Well, I do have plans, but…”
It’s not like I’m just playing around.
After all, the main reason I quit the archery club is because I wanted to prioritize work.

親父が他界した後、生活費ぐらいは自分で出すとアルバイトを始めてもう五年。
それだけ色んな仕事をしていると、断れない付き合いというのも出てきてしまう。

pages.en:
After my father died, I decided to cover at least my own living expenses. I began working five years ago.

Once you have held that many different jobs, you inevitably acquire obligations that are difficult to refuse.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It’s already been five years since Father died, and I decided to start working to pay my living expenses.
If you work a lot, there are some jobs you just can’t refuse.

pages.en:
Today's engagement is precisely that sort.

A local pub is taking inventory. They asked me to come if possible, since the more men they have to lift things, the better.

Still, it is not work that specifically requires *me*. In truth, they are merely gathering acquaintances because everyone wants to celebrate once the inventory is finished.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Today’s an example.
They’re restocking inventory at work, and they asked me to come if I can as any help is appreciated.
But it’s certainly not something I have to go to. They’re probably just having people come in because they want to party after work.
